summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and chronic obstructive lung disease, was admitted due to acute hypoxia and increased oxygen requirements after a sudden onset of shortness of breath at home. Initial concern for pneumonia was raised due to new left upper lobe opacities on chest imaging, prompting initiation of broad-spectrum antibiotics. However, lack of fever, leukocytosis, and negative follow-up blood cultures led to discontinuation of antibiotics, with the episode attributed to reactive airways and poor secretion clearance rather than active infection. She completed a course of meropenem for a previously diagnosed ESBL urinary tract infection. The PICC line was removed due to a single positive blood culture for coagulase-negative Staphylococcus, later deemed a contaminant. Imaging revealed stable findings including a soft tissue mass in the azygoesophageal recess and right hilar lymphadenopathy, with recommendations for follow-up. The patient stabilized on oxygen support and was discharged home with her PCA, on adjusted medications including increased levothyroxine and modified pain and bladder regimens.
